prototype: output/sessions/2026-08/2026-08-17_dcs-homepage-redesign/prototype/r9-kota-level.html, copied to sites/dcs/public/__parity__/ so both documents share one origin, and deleted again before this phase commits.

harness.shape: Two same-origin Playwright pages, each given an explicit context viewport, driven in lockstep. The brief's two-iframe shape is not usable: the built site ships X-Frame-Options: DENY and frame-ancestors 'none', so it cannot be framed without either weakening the app's security headers or rewriting CSP in flight — and rewriting CSP would invalidate behavioural assertion 11, whose whole job is to prove there are zero CSP violations. Trap 7's point (resize_window reports success and does nothing) is satisfied a different way: the viewport is set on the context, and every snapshot records the in-page innerWidth/innerHeight as evidence that it actually applied.
harness.scrollDiscipline: Both pages are parked at the same scrollY before either is read, and the layout pass measures both at scrollY 0 in one synchronous in-page evaluation each. The previous run measured the two documents at different scroll offsets, which made every position:fixed and every display:none element report a spurious delta equal to the mismatch (~3543px) — that cluster was a harness artefact, not a layout regression.
harness.positionBasis: topInSection uses the prototype layoutTop() sticky/fixed neutralisation (Trap 4) relative to the nearest .panel/.hero/.bar/.menu ancestor. Where that section is itself position:fixed, a viewport basis is used, because a fixed section has no document position for its descendants to be relative to. Both bases are scroll-independent.
harness.revealLatch: Both pages are walked through their full scroll range in lockstep before measurement so every .panel latches its one-shot .in class in both. Without it, .res colour is a race between the two IntersectionObservers and reads differently run to run.
harness.evidence: Every number comes from getComputedStyle/getBoundingClientRect, never from pixels (Trap 2). Nothing reads a live rAF-written value (Trap 1): the nav ground is recomputed from live rects by a pure port of the prototype ground(), and the DOM attribute is cross-checked against that computation rather than trusted. elementFromPoint is never used (Trap 3). Every page load is cache-busted (Trap 6).

normalisation.fontFamily: next/font hashed families are canonicalised (__Archivo_ab12 -> archivo) and the generated metrics-matched *_Fallback_* face is dropped. DECISION: normalised away, not counted as a failure. next/font/google injects a size-adjusted local fallback purely to hold the box steady during the font swap; the primary face is what renders once loaded, and the zero-delta widths and heights recorded here are the evidence that the fallback introduces no shift. Treating it as a hard fail would make this gate permanently unpassable for any next/font site, which cannot be the intent of a parity gate.
normalisation.notRenderedAtViewport: Elements with no client rects are compared for PRESENCE parity and then skipped: .hero__m, .tiercards and .tcard are display:none above 900px and .menu is hidden until opened, and a display:none element has no box to compare. A rendered-ness mismatch between the two documents is a hard failure.

allowList.summary: Line boxes containing "→" are 1px shorter in the port and the glyph ~1.2px narrower.
allowList.reason: next/font's metrics-matched fallback doing its job. U+2192 is outside Archivo's latin subset, so the glyph comes from the next family in the stack: `system-ui` in the standalone prototype, next/font's size-adjusted `Archivo Fallback` in the port. Measured directly — with the arrow stripped the same element is 44px in BOTH documents; with the arrow alone it is 44px in the port and 45px in the prototype. Only two elements on the page contain the character (.wpanel__l "npracingbsb.co.uk ->" and "smcommercial.uk ->", and .svccard__l "Start a project ->"); every entry below is that 1px propagating through the grid rows around them. Disabling `adjustFontFallback` to chase a 1px match would reintroduce exactly the layout-shift risk next/font exists to prevent, for a difference that is not visible at rest — and the prototype's own value is platform-dependent, since it is whatever the visitor's OS supplies for system-ui, where the port's is pinned to a face size-adjusted to Archivo.
allowList.costOfMatchingTheReference: adjustFontFallback: false on Archivo and Poppins in app/layout.tsx. Not taken.

alsoAffectsBehavioural.note: The two .wpanel__l links measure 43px tall in the port against the prototype's 44px, so they cross a 44px touch-target floor the prototype clears by exactly 1px. Same single cause; no other target differs.

allowList.summary: The mobile eCommerce card's <button class="btn"> is 50px in the port against 54px in the prototype.
allowList.reason: A defect in the reference prototype, not a design intent. The prototype is a standalone HTML file whose only reset is `*{box-sizing:border-box;margin:0;padding:0}`, so its one <button class="btn"> (the mobile eCommerce card's "See upfront pricing", the only .btn on the page that is not an <a>) keeps Chrome's UA `border: 2px outset` — captured and inspected during this phase, it renders as a black bevelled ring around the magenta pill. Tailwind Preflight removes it in the port. Reproducing it would ship a visible regression against the rest of the r9 design language, in which no other CTA carries a border, to satisfy a measurement. The 4px height difference on that one button is the whole of this entry; everything else below is it propagating up through .tcard#3, .tiercards, the pricing .panel and the three cornerfills beneath it.
allowList.costOfMatchingTheReference: border-style: revert; border-width: revert on the control block in styles/home-r9-reset.css. Not taken.

behavioural.description: Nav ground matches the prototype at 61 sampled scroll positions with both pages parked at the same scrollY, the live DOM data-ground agrees with the pure recomputation at every sample, magenta holds across all six service cards, and the process panel cuts to ink.

All in-page menu and footer links land their target at top:0 when clicked from the page bottom — the only position where the unbounded-sticky bug reproduces, and the one that makes native anchor navigation a no-op.

The pricing detail pane is the same height in every reachable tier/pay-mode state with the CTA at the same offset in all of them (range 0), the seven reachable states are exactly the seven the prototype reaches, and the tier figures are right-aligned in all eight tier/mode combinations. Below 900px the pane is display:none by design, so there only the state machine and the alignment are asserted.

Selecting eCommerce while the monthly tab is active switches the pay mode to upfront — there is no monthly price for a store, so that state is unreachable by design rather than showing a dead N/A pane.

All five work panels pin — bounding-box top held at 0 across a measured scroll span — including the LAST one, which is the one that silently stops pinning if .wstack::after is missing, and every panel pins for exactly the same span as in the prototype.

The burger overlay opens to the full viewport rather than to the bar's own box. A trapped overlay reports the bar's box instead, which is the signature of a backdrop-filter or transform ancestor establishing the containing block.

Every section-curve cornerfill reads the colour of the pane above it, identically to the prototype, at every boundary the page actually has (7 — the brief said 8, the markup has 7 in BOTH documents, so the count itself is at parity).

The comma'd prices £1,495 and £2,995 resolve, up the whole ancestor chain, to a non-mono family and inherit no tabular-nums. Either would give the comma a full digit advance and render the figure as £1 , 495.

At 390px and at 320px the homepage has no horizontal overflow, no prose below the 16px floor, and no interactive target under 44px that the PROTOTYPE does not also have OR that is not accounted for by a documented allow-list entry (the two .wpanel__l arrow links, 43px against the prototype's 44px — see allowList[u2192-font-fallback]). Measured on both documents rather than as an absolute, because this phase gates the port against its reference: an undersized target present identically in both is a property of the approved design, not a regression introduced by the port. Both lists are recorded in full. Scoped to the r9 furniture — the consent manager and analytics debug panel are root-layout chrome, not part of this port — and WCAG 2.5.8's inline-text exception is recorded rather than silently dropped.

The comma'd prices £1,495 and £2,995 resolve, up the whole ancestor chain, to a non-mono family and inherit no tabular-nums. Either would give the comma a full digit advance and render the figure as £1 , 495.

The hero headline is present in the server-rendered HTML before any JS runs: the per-character split happens during React render, not in a useEffect. Rendering it empty until script fires is the one thing the reference site the prototype is measured against gets wrong, so this is the assertion the whole hero was built for.

Zero CSP violations, zero console errors and zero failed responses across both viewport runs, with every R2 asset URL the built page requests returning 200 (or 206, the correct success status for the <video> range requests).
